Audiometry is normal (no hearing loss or tinnitus), neurological exam has no focal deficits, and head imaging is normal (no central lesion). These findings strongly favor a peripheral, positionally triggered cause—classically benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). The pattern of provocation (left Dix–Hallpike positive) localizes to the left posterior semicircular canal (canalithiasis). 

DIAGNOSIS: Left posterior canal benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)
